benchmark.source: Cook County Assessor (Open Data)
benchmark.scope: all residential improvement records

benchmark.source: DC Office of Tax and Revenue (Open Data)
benchmark.scope: non-condominium homes only (condos are ~36% of DC's CAMA stock)

benchmark.source: DC Office of Tax and Revenue (Open Data)
benchmark.scope: condominium units only (61,329 of DC's 170,602 CAMA records)

benchmark.source: NJOGIS Parcels and MOD-IV Composite of New Jersey
benchmark.scope: residential (class 2) parcels in all 21 counties, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Contra Costa, San Joaquin and Riverside County Assessors
benchmark.scope: residential parcels and condominium units in the three counties, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Los Angeles County Office of the Assessor (LA County eGIS parcels)
benchmark.scope: parcels the roll classifies Residential, condominium units included and typed with their unit

benchmark.source: NYC Department of City Planning MapPLUTO (Department of Finance)
benchmark.scope: tax lots with at least one residential unit in all five boroughs, drawn in proportion to each borough's housing units (a condominium is one billing lot)

benchmark.source: San Francisco Office of the Assessor-Recorder (DataSF secured roll)
benchmark.scope: residential records (single- and multi-family uses, condominium units included) in the latest closed secured roll

benchmark.source: Texas county appraisal districts (twelve counties' own services)
benchmark.scope: residential accounts (state categories A single-family and condominium, B multifamily, M mobile homes) in the twelve counties the adapter serves, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Denver, Jefferson, Adams, Douglas and Boulder county assessors
benchmark.scope: residential parcels (houses, condominium units, townhouses and multifamily) in the five Denver-metro counties the adapter serves, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: MetroGIS Regional Parcel Dataset (Metropolitan Council)
benchmark.scope: residential parcels (houses, townhouses, condominium units, duplexes to apartments) in the seven metro counties, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Connecticut GIS Office statewide CAMA and parcel layer
benchmark.scope: residential parcels with a year built in all nine planning regions, drawn in proportion to each region's housing units

benchmark.source: Jackson County (MO) Assessment Department Parcel Viewer
benchmark.scope: dwelling land-use records (houses, townhouses, condominium units, duplexes to apartments) in Jackson County, the one county the adapter serves

benchmark.source: SEMCOG Building Footprints 2024
benchmark.scope: live single-family, attached-condo and apartment buildings (not parcels) in Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw, Livingston, St. Clair and Monroe, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Chesterfield County Open GIS Data; City of Richmond Assessor
benchmark.scope: residential assessment records in Chesterfield County and the City of Richmond only, drawn in proportion to each one's housing units

benchmark.source: MassGIS Level 3 standardized assessor parcels
benchmark.scope: records with a residential DOR use code in all 351 cities and towns (condominium units included, typed with their unit), drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: NYS ITS Geospatial Services public tax parcels (ORPTS rolls)
benchmark.scope: residential (class 2xx) parcels in the 33 opted-in counties outside New York City, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units; homes the roll gives no year built are counted, not skipped

benchmark.source: Philadelphia Office of Property Assessment (OpenDataPhilly, Carto)
benchmark.scope: OPA accounts in the dwelling categories (single family, multi family, mixed use, apartments), condominium units included

benchmark.source: NC OneMap statewide parcels (county tax offices)
benchmark.scope: parcels the adapter reads as homes with a year built, in the 46 of 100 counties that record one (64% of the state's housing units), drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Fulton, Clayton, Chatham (SAGIS) and Forsyth county parcel layers
benchmark.scope: improved residential parcels in the four counties the adapter answers for (19% of Georgia's homes), drawn in proportion to each county's housing units
benchmark.assessment_year: 2024-2026 by county (Fulton 2026, Chatham 2025, Forsyth 2024, Clayton current)

benchmark.source: Maryland SDAT assessment data on MD iMAP parcel boundaries
benchmark.scope: residential parcel polygons with a premise address and a year built in all 23 counties and Baltimore City, drawn in proportion to housing units; condominium units filed only as account points (~150,000) are outside it

benchmark.source: Florida Department of Revenue statewide cadastral (county property appraisers' rolls)
benchmark.scope: residential parcels (DOR use 001-008) with a dwelling unit and a year built in all 67 counties, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: UGRC Land Information Records parcels (Utah county tax rolls)
benchmark.scope: residential parcels with a recorded year built in the 28 counties served, one draw per parcel, in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Allegheny County Office of Property Assessments (WPRDC)
benchmark.scope: roll records with a dwelling land use (houses, townhouses, rowhouses, condominium units, two- to four-family, apartments, farms), placed on the county parcel layer

benchmark.source: Montgomery, York, Northampton and Cumberland County (PA) assessment parcel layers
benchmark.scope: residential parcels with a recorded year built in Montgomery, York, Northampton and Cumberland counties, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Ohio county auditors' parcel layers (nine counties)
benchmark.scope: residential, agricultural and apartment parcels with a recorded year built in the nine counties served, drawn in proportion to each county's housing units

benchmark.source: Vanderburgh County Assessor tax parcels
benchmark.scope: residential, apartment and farmhouse parcels with a recorded year built in Vanderburgh County
